hero_quote_2_egipte_malta: Yes, there are towns called Egypt and Malta in Latvia. We're not sure what's the story there, but we're sure that these are some of the best gravel roads Northern Europe has to offer.
hero_quote_2_parize_dakara: Route inspired by Paris - Dakar rally. Just like the rally ended at the Westernmost tip of Africa, this route will end at Latvia's Westernmost point along the Baltic coast. Along the way you'll visit Paris as well. Some say you might even spot the Eiffel tower.
faq_contact_prompt: Didn't find the answer to your question?
faq_a1: Pasaules Tūre (eng. World Tour) organizes gravel cycling events in Latvia. The theme of each event is to visit places in Latvia that reference famous locations around the world.
faq_q2: What type of bicycle do I need?
faq_a2: A gravel or MTB will be most suitable.
faq_q3: What is included in the participation fee?
faq_a3: Photos, food at checkpoints, snacks and drinks at the finish, bag storage / transportation, tested gpx file. Other things may differ from event to event.
faq_q4: What is available at the start/finish?
faq_a4: At Egypt-Malta event it is possible to overnight in Sarkankalns at no extra cost (15 pers.) There will be coffee at the start and at the finish line we’ll wait for you with drinks and snacks. You’ll be able to wash both your bike and yourself at the finish and in Sarkankalns a sauna will be available.
faq_a5: At the checkpoints you will find good food, snacks, drinks and checkpoint postage stamps.
faq_q6: What happens if I decide to withdraw?
faq_a6: First, let the organizers know. Afterwards, you’ll have to make your own way home or to the finish. If we will be nearby, we will help, but don't count on that.
faq_a7: If you want to compete and go fast - go for it! If you want to enjoy it and ride at your own pace - that’s great! There’s a relaxed atmosphere at Pasaules Tūre where everyone can decide their own adventure.
faq_a8: Yes! Party pace is the place to be.
faq_q9: This will be my first ultra. How can I prepare?
faq_a9: If you have any questions, need advice or words of encouragement, reach out to us!
faq_a10: Bike bag(s), helmet, repair kit, weather appropriate clothing, bike lights, navigation device (phone or bike computer). A precise list of mandatory equipment is sent out to registered participants before the event. If you don't have your own bike bags, contact us! We have bikepacking bags available for rent.
faq_a11: There is a time limit for checkpoints, but it is generous enough so that everyone can make it in time. Finish will remain open until the last participant.
faq_a12: If you cancel less than 14 days before the event no refund will be made. If you cancel less than 30 days before the event, you’ll be refunded 50%. If you cancel more than 30 days before the event, you’ll be refunded 100%.
faq_q13: Can I transfer my participation to someone else?
faq_a13: Yes you can. Email us with a name, surname and email of the new participant.

plan_em_1_title: I. The day before the start
plan_em_2_body: The day before the start, you're welcome to come to Sarkaņkalns. There's parking, a kitchen, showers, places to relax, peace and fresh air in scenic surroundings, and even a small beach by Adamova lake. The spot is 9km from the train station. Trains leave Riga at 08:01, 12:01, and 17:01, arriving in Rēzekne at 11:23, 14:50, and 20:27 respectively.
plan_em_3_caption: The way to Sarkaņkalns from Rēzekne train station
plan_em_4_body: Everyone who marked during registration that they want to stay in the cabin will get a mattress. Just bring your own sleeping bag and pillow. The rest will have a big yard for pitching tents. The cabin can actually fit a lot of people, but we capped the spots so it's easier to spread out and get a proper night's sleep. Spend the evening before the start however you like, but quiet hours start at 22:00.
plan_em_6_title: II. The morning of the start
plan_em_7_body: During the morning we welcome the rest of the riders and open registration. Everyone gets a postcard and a keepsake photo. At each checkpoint volunteers will stick a stamp on your postcard — a little souvenir from the ride.
plan_em_9_body: The ride starts at 9:00. Just before that, the organizer will go over the most important rules and lead riders through the first few kilometers as a neutralized start.
plan_em_11_lead: From 9:00 on June 6 until the finish
plan_em_11_body: During the event, everyone rides at their own pace and on their own terms. For some it'll be just another ride, for many the biggest one yet. Our goal is to encourage anyone to take part and create an environment where every rider feels welcome and supported. In the first year, every participant managed to finish by Sunday evening. This year we've also added a shorter distance option, finishing in Daugavpils.
plan_em_13_body: Both distances share a checkpoint in the courtyard of the Egypt church ruins. There'll be a tent set up, with snacks and drinks, warm triangle pastries, and power to charge your devices. During daylight hours volunteers will be there to greet you and cheer you on; at night the checkpoint stays lit and runs on a self-serve basis.
plan_em_15_body: Riders on the full distance will have one more checkpoint in Aglona, just before Malta. The exact spot will be confirmed before the start, but expect a guesthouse, snacks, and drinks. Some riders might reach this checkpoint at night or early morning when shops aren't open yet, so it'll be a great spot for a short rest.
plan_em_16_body: The shorter distance ends at Stropu lake in Daugavpils where participants will have access to facilities with a shower and a place to rest. The organizers can transport your belongings from Sarkaņkalns to here. From Daugavpils you can take a train to Riga or a bus back to Rēzekne. The full distance ends at Sarkaņkalns, where there's also a sauna. At the finish for both distances refreshing drinks from Labieties brewery.
plan_pd_2_body: Participants are welcome from 8:00 AM at Stacija Vaivari pizzeria, located just a few metres from Vaivari railway station. Coffee, tea, and a selection of snacks will be available, giving everyone a chance to wake up, fuel up, and settle into the day. A few minutes before the 9:00 AM start, the event organizer, Toms, will go over the most important points from the event manual, which will be sent to all participants no later than one week before the event. Then, the adventure begins.
plan_pd_3_caption: The start at Stacija Vaivari pizzeria
plan_pd_4_body: Not long after the start, riders will enter Ķemeri National Park, where they'll pass through the historic Ķemeri Resort Park and ride alongside the impressive Green Dune ridge. And if anyone is still feeling sleepy, the rolling hills around Tukums city will soon wake up their legs before rewarding the effort with the beautiful Abava River Valley.
plan_pd_5_body: The first checkpoint will be located near Buses Hillfort, almost exactly at the 100 km mark. The exact details will be confirmed later, but as with every World Tour event, you can expect a warm welcome from friendly volunteers who will be there to cheer you on. And naturally, there will be plenty of snacks and drinks waiting as well.
plan_pd_6_body: From there, the route crosses into neighbouring Lithuania and heads for Mažeikiai, where, surprisingly enough, the locals have hidden their very own little Paris—complete with its iconic Eiffel Tower. Don't forget to bring your passport or national ID card! This will be a photo checkpoint, where participants must send the organizers a photo taken at the Eiffel Tower. Group photos are perfectly fine, and tagging us in an Instagram Story works too. The funniest and most creative submissions will earn a small prize.
plan_pd_6_caption: The Eiffel Tower in the local Paris
plan_pd_7_body: Most participants will reach Mažeikiai during the afternoon or evening. As it's a reasonably large town, it's also an excellent place to spend the night for anyone who prefers not to ride through the dark—with more than half of the route already behind them.
plan_pd_8_body: The second half of the route takes you through the scenic South Kurzeme region, an area many cyclists rarely have the chance to explore. After another checkpoint in Priekule, the journey concludes on the Baltic Sea coast in Bernāti. Just a short distance from the finish lies Latvia's westernmost point. Staying true to the Paris–Dakar rally theme, this location serves as a symbolic counterpart to Dakar, home to the westernmost point of the African continent.
plan_pd_9_caption: Stone monument near Latvia's westernmost point.
plan_pd_10_body: At the finish, participants will have access to showers, and those arriving during the night will have a place to get some rest. The organizers will also transport participants' bags to the finish. For the return journey to Riga, trains depart from Liepāja on Sunday at 4:57 AM and 5:55 PM. There are also regular bus services, which typically have space for bicycles in the luggage compartment.
